newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BankWatch downgrades debt ratings on S.Korea banks.
newsitem.headline: BankWatch downgrades debt ratings on S.Korea banks.

text.p: New York-based Thomson BankWatch Inc has downgraded its risk ratings on South Korea and its banks, a statement received on Wednesday said.
The ratings agency said it lowered the Sovereign Risk on South Korea to A+ from AA- because Thomson BankWatch was losing confidence for the current government to contain mounting economic pressures.

"Faced with a sharp slowdown in economic growth, slumping exports, ballooning deficits on both the trade and current accounts, and rapidly mounting foreign debt, the outlook for the South Korean economy remains gloomy," the statement said.
The agency also lowered ratings on five South Korean commercial banks -- Korea Exchange Bank, Hanil Bank, Cho Hung Bank, Commercial Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK.
The downgrades reflected concerns over deteriorating asset quality, taking into account prospects for a significant slowing in the overall economy, it said.
Those banks were also hit by an increasing competitiveness on the local market and unrealised losses in their securities holdings, BankWatch said.
Following are details of downgraded ratings by BankWatch:
Korea Exchange: intra-country issuer lowered to IC-C from IC-B/C and short-term affirmed at LC-1. (IC stands for intra-country and LC for local currency).
Hanil: intra-country issuer lowered to IC-C/D from IC-C and short-term LC lowered to LC-2 from LC-1.
Cho Hung: intra-country issuer affirmed at IC-C/D and short-term LC lowered to LC-2 from LC-1.
Commercial Bank: intra-country issuer affirmed at IC-C/D and short-term LC lowered to LC-2 from LC-1.
SEOULBANK: intra-country issuer lowered to IC-D from IC-C/D and short-term LC lowered to LC-3 from LC-1.
